newsitem.title: USA: Four senators going to W. House on airline dispute.
newsitem.headline: Four senators going to W. House on airline dispute.

text.p: Four senators planned Wednesday to go to the White House to express concerns about the disruptions a strike by American Airlines pilots would cause.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Sens. Dick Durbin, D-Ill., Bob Graham, D-Fla., Kay Bailey Hutchinson, R-Texas, and Barbara Boxer, D-Calif., would meet White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles in the afternoon.
They are from states that serve as hubs for American Airlines, a unit of AMR Corp..
A strike by the 9,000 pilots for the country's No. 2 carrier would occur at midnight Friday unless a new contract can be reached.
A strike would disrupt travel for the 200,000 passengers the carrier flies on its 2,200 routes worldwide every day.

McCurry said the senators want to "express their own concern about what a disruption this would be for airline travel if there is a strike (and) review with the White House what procedures exist under the Railway Labour Act for taking steps if the current effort by the National Mediation Board does not produce a fruitful outcome."
President Clinton can intervene and declare a national emergency under the Railway Labour Act in order to keep the planes flying.
"Obviously we're greatly concerned about the status of negotiations," McCurry said.
Asked if Clinton was inclined to take those steps if no contract is reached, McCurry said: "I'm not going to speculate."
